title: cost-curator-cli: simulate tenant unit-econ scenarios and propose conservative batch/cache/quant defaults
author: Priya Malhotra
body:
Summary: Adds a new cost-curator CLI tool and server-side support to simulate tenant-level unit economics under different batching, KV cache, and quantization presets, then emit conservative suggestions that are safe to roll out. Motivation: customers frequently ask for concrete defaults they can apply without running full load tests. The goal is to make a lightweight, repeatable way to project cost/latency impact and produce conservative presets that minimize downstream regressions.

What this PR includes: - a new CLI (redwood cli cost-curator simulate) that loads a tenant's sample traces or synthetic workload and runs deterministic cost/latency simulations for combinations of: microbatch size, prefill strategy, KV cache hit rates, and quantization profiles - an offline simulator service (lightweight python worker) used by the CLI for faster local dry-runs - a suggestion engine that ranks candidate presets by a conservative utility score prioritizing no-latency-regressions and cost reduction - safety checks and rollback keys: suggestions include a compatibility fingerprint and an automatic guardrail that disallows suggested quant profiles for known-sensitive families (e.g., older Llama variants) - telemetry events and metrics (cost_curator.simulation_start, cost_curator.suggestion, estimated_tokens_saved, expected_p50_latency_ms) - docs and examples including a tenant dry-run guide and a CI-friendly --dry-run --ci flags for automation.

Design notes: The simulator is deterministic: it replays sample request size distribution, sequence length histogram, and per-route qps. It uses conservative estimates for KV cache fill/evict behavior to avoid optimistic wins. Quantization impact is modeled using precomputed degradation profiles per model family (collected from prior bench runs) and a confidence band. The suggestion engine applies a simple multi-criteria scoring function with tunable weights: safety_weight, cost_weight, latency_weight.

Checklist: - [x] CLI parsing and help text - [x] Simulator worker and model family profiles - [x] Suggestion ranking and compatibility fingerprints - [x] Unit tests for scoring and fallback logic - [x] Integration smoke test that runs against a small sample trace - [x] Docs and examples - [x] Telemetry and metrics emitted

Testing: added unit tests (pytest) for scoring, a small integration harness that runs the CLI against the sample-tenant fixture, and a perf micro-benchmark to ensure the simulator completes within acceptable time for local runs (~8s for a 1k request sample). CI: full test matrix passed after two reruns of flaky test related to kv-eviction sim.

Rollout plan: feature is behind feature flag cost_curator.preview_cli. Default rollout: enable for internal tenants and opt-in for early access customers. Suggestions are only exported; they are not applied automatically. Next step after this PR: add a service endpoint for automated tenant heuristic sweeps and a web UI to view suggested presets.

Backwards compatibility: CLI is additive. No existing API surface was changed. Suggestions include compatibility fingerprints to avoid accidental application on incompatible model families.

Metrics to watch post-rollout: cost_curator.suggestion.accept_rate, estimated_tokens_saved (sum), p50_latency_change for tenants that accept suggestions.

Related work: ENG-2145 (tenant warmstart experiments), ENG-2182 (quant profile canonicalization).

2b3c4d5 - simulator: deterministic replay engine and conservative kv model
3c4d5e6 - suggestor: scoring function and compatibility fingerprint
4d5e6f7 - docs: add cost-curator CLI guide and examples
5e6f7a8 - tests: unit + integration harness and CI flakiness fixes
review_comments: 2026-02-11 Daniel White: Can we keep the default suggestion conservative? The scoring weight should bias to zero-latency-regression. — replied: acknowledged, added safety_weight=0.6 default and tests.

2026-02-12 Marta Kovács: Are the precomputed quant degradation profiles updatable? Might need a migration path. — replied: yes, profiles are versioned under pkg/profiles and we added a simple migrate_profiles script.
2026-02-13 Lina Ortega: Please add telemetry event naming and ensure GDPR-safe payloads. — replied: updated events.py to strip tenant PII and added unit test.
2026-02-14 Daniel White: Small nit: flag name should be --dry-run not --dry. — resolved in commit 3c4d5e6.
release_notes: Add cost-curator CLI and offline simulator to generate conservative batching/caching/quant suggestions. CLI supports --dry-run and --ci flags. Suggestions are opt-in and feature-gated. Emits telemetry for adoption tracking.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated (cost_curator.preview_cli). Monitor suggestion.accept_rate and estimated_tokens_saved. Ensure quant_profiles.yaml is deployed on all inference fleet nodes before enabling for customers.
testing_summary: Unit tests (scoring, compat), integration smoke test against sample tenant trace, and CI runs. Two flaky tests were rerun and stabilized. Local simulator completes ~8s for 1k requests sample on dev laptop.
priority_risks: Quantization suggestions may still have edge-case regressions for very old model variants; guardrails added but recommend manual verification before tenant-wide application.
eg_usage_examples:
# dry-run against a local sample trace
redwood cli cost-curator simulate --trace examples/cost_curator/sample_tenant_trace.json --dry-run

# CI friendly run that writes suggestion.json
redwood cli cost-curator simulate --trace examples/cost_curator/sample_tenant_trace.json --ci --out suggestions.json
